EO-01.mapping_to_concept: MAESTRO directly addresses this outcome through Pillar 1 (Neuro-Symbolic Planning and Reasoning) and Pillar 2 (Adaptive Memory Architecture), unified by the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer. Pillar 1 develops a hybrid planning engine combining LLM-based reasoning with formal symbolic planning, producing verifiable sub-task decomposition, plan monitoring, and self-correction mechanisms that directly constitute improvements in planning mechanisms and reasoning capabilities. Pillar 2 designs a three-tier memory architecture (working, episodic, semantic) with a memory controller that explicitly addresses memory management for long-horizon coherent agent behaviour. The External Tool and API Orchestration Layer provides post-invocation verification and automated fallback/recovery mechanisms that directly enhance agent robustness and reliability. Strategic_positioning.md (lines 14–17) explicitly frames MAESTRO's response to this outcome: 'MAESTRO addresses this through Pillars 1 (neuro-symbolic planning and reasoning) and 2 (adaptive memory architecture).'

EO-07.mapping_to_concept: MAESTRO directly addresses this outcome through Pillar 3 (Decentralised Multi-Agent Coordination), extended by the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer's multi-agent tool governance capabilities. EO-01.strategic_differentiation: The proposal's research differentiation is the defensible end-to-end coupling of three capabilities the reviewed literature reports as underdeveloped in combination: (1) learned multimodal fusion of multi-source Earth observation (Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, PlanetScope high-resolution imagery, ERA5 meteorological reanalysis) and field sensors, (2) explicit probabilistic crop-water-state estimation (root-zone soil moisture and crop water status for tomato, with uncertainty carried honestly from observation through the model), and (3) water-use-efficiency-oriented irrigation decision optimisation via uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration and counterfactual simulation over weather ensembles. The targeted novelty occupies the single empty cell in the systematic literature review's research-gap matrix — Real-Time Decision Support × PlanetScope — argued narrowly and defended against 50 reviewed studies rather than asserted. The methodological commitment distinguishing this proposal from related work is the honest uncertainty chain from multi-sensor observation to irrigation decision: every model output reports not only what the field state is but how certain that estimate is, and that uncertainty propagates all the way into the decision. Objectives are measurable against a defined validation protocol (90% prediction-interval coverage on the validation set as the calibration criterion; Route B patch covariation proven by co-located seasonal campaign), not merely asserted. The researcher-and-host differentiation rests on a unique disciplinary pairing unavailable in a single-discipline fellowship: Dr. Rositsa Cholakova (plant physiologist, non-destructive evaluation of drought-stressed tomato plants — PhD summa cum laude 2020 — provides the biological ground truth engine, RQ4) is hosted in the geoinformatics and remote sensing group at ELTE Budapest under Dr. András Jung (remote sensing, hyperspectral imaging, field spectroscopy, multisensor-drone fusion), creating a genuine two-way knowledge transfer in which neither partner's disciplinary capability alone is sufficient for the end-to-end framework. The proposal is framed as a European Fellowship at ELTE Budapest, Hungary (intra-EU, Bulgaria → Hungary, 24 months), with Earth-observation data access confirmed (PlanetScope via Planet platform/API; Sentinel-1/2 open data; ERA5 reanalysis) and Hungarian tomato field access secured via associated partner AgroVIR. Research output is a TRL 3–4 research prototype, proportionate to a 24-month fellowship and appropriate to the novelty claim.

strategic_differentiation: MAESTRO's primary differentiator within the call scope is the architectural co-design of three mutually reinforcing research pillars — neuro-symbolic planning and reasoning (Pillar 1), adaptive memory architecture (Pillar 2), and decentralised multi-agent coordination (Pillar 3) — unified by a cross-cutting External Tool and API Orchestration Layer, as a single integrated system rather than a combination of independently developed components. Existing AI agent approaches operate from three disconnected research communities: LLM-based agents (strong on natural language understanding, weak on long-horizon planning robustness), classical planning and multi-agent systems (strong on formal guarantees, weak on open-ended real-world tasks), and memory-augmented neural systems (focused on single-turn retrieval accuracy, lacking planning and coordination integration). MAESTRO's co-design principle means the planning engine uses the memory architecture to maintain coherence over long task horizons; the multi-agent protocol uses both planning and memory to coordinate heterogeneous agents; and the tool orchestration layer is architecturally integrated across all three pillars with a typed tool registry, formal selection policies, standardised adapters, post-invocation verification, and auditable traces — rather than being a simple function-calling interface bolted on as an afterthought. The neuro-symbolic approach provides formal planning guarantees (verifiable sub-task decomposition, provable convergence for multi-agent delegation protocols) not achievable by pure LLM-based systems, directly differentiating MAESTRO from prompt-engineering-based agent frameworks and LLM wrapper architectures. Validation spans two call-identified Apply AI sectors (healthcare clinical decision support and advanced manufacturing process optimisation) with full operational demonstrators co-designed with sector-leading industry partners, plus a cross-sector logistics and supply chain transfer demonstrator confirming architectural portability and generalisability beyond the minimum sector requirement. The consortium combines leading European AI research institutions, sector-specific industry partners providing real deployment environments, and a technology transfer partner ensuring framework adoption through the AI-on-demand platform and EDIHs.
